newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian parliament speaker blocks two decrees.
newsitem.headline: Italian parliament speaker blocks two decrees.

text.p: The speaker of Italy's lower house of parliament on Wednesday blocked two of six decrees the government added to the 1997 budget package.
Chamber of Deputies Speaker Luciano Violante ruled that the two decrees, on health and pensions, could not be part of the budget bill and must be presented as separate draft bills.

Opposition parties, which are boycotting the budget debate in protest against government demands for special powers to dictate policy without recourse to parliament, blasted the decision to add the decrees.

Under a recent court ruling, the government is barred from continuing the traditional practice of re-issuing expiring decrees. Instead, they have to be converted into law by parliament within 60 days or dropped.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has already called several confidence votes to turn expiring decrees into law.
Attaching the decrees to the budget enables the government to keep potentially dangerous confidence votes to a minimum.
